facts.raw_span: A 30-year-old woman presented with a large unhealed ulcer measuring 20 × 14-cm² that had persisted for the past 3 years
a patch of healthy skin (7.5 × 4 cm²) on her left forearm
Blood cell genotyping revealed compound heterozygous alterations (c.2992 + 2T>G and c.8621-30A>G) at splice sites in COL7A1
A 20 × 14-cm² persistent ulcer on the back
A patch of healthy skin (7.5 × 4 cm²) on the left forearm, lacking blistering
Blood cell genotyping showed compound heterozygous alterations in COL7A1
RNA transcript analysis using MinION platform:  * Affected skin epidermis: Dominant RNA transcripts with premature stop codons, wild-type reads rare (1.1%)
Potentially revertant area epidermis: High rates of wild-type transcripts (35.0%)
Revertant skin dermis: Wild-type reads rare (1.9%)
Immunofluorescence and transmission electron microscopy of the grafted area showed type VII collagen and anchoring fibrils
Figure 1A: Sanger sequencing showing compound heterozygous COL7A1 alteration
Figure 1B: Image of the persistent ulcer on patient's back

concepts.why: The patient's compound heterozygous COL7A1 alterations and the presence of type VII collagen and anchoring fibril defects support this diagnosis.
The high rates of wild-type transcripts in the potentially revertant area epidermis and the presence of a patch of healthy skin suggest this diagnosis.
The patient's large unhealed ulcer and the presence of a persistent ulcer on the back support this diagnosis.
The patient's compound heterozygous COL7A1 alterations and the presence of type VII collagen defects support this diagnosis.
The patient's genetic mutations and skin lesions support this diagnosis.
The presence of anchoring fibril defects supports this diagnosis.

rationales.F01: The presence of a large unhealed ulcer suggests a chronic condition such as Dystrophic Epidermolysis Bullosa.
rationales.F02: The presence of a patch of healthy skin on the left forearm suggests Revertant Mosaicism in Epidermolysis Bullosa.
rationales.F03: The compound heterozygous alterations in COL7A1 are a strong indicator of Dystrophic Epidermolysis Bullosa and Collagen VII Deficiency.
rationales.F06: The blood cell genotyping results confirm the presence of COL7A1 alterations, supporting the diagnosis of Dystrophic Epidermolysis Bullosa and Collagen VII Deficiency.
rationales.F07: The RNA transcript analysis results suggest that the affected skin epidermis has dominant RNA transcripts with premature stop codons, which is consistent with Dystrophic Epidermolysis Bullosa.
rationales.F08: The high rates of wild-type transcripts in the potentially revertant area epidermis suggest Revertant Mosaicism in Epidermolysis Bullosa.
rationales.F10: The presence of type VII collagen and anchoring fibrils in the grafted area is consistent with Dystrophic Epidermolysis Bullosa and Collagen VII Deficiency.
